interpretation.rate: Sinus tachycardia at ~99 bpm. Elevated compared to prior recording (78 bpm). Multiple possible causes: anxiety, pain, fever, hypovolemia, medications, physical activity prior to recording.
interpretation.rhythm: Regular sinus rhythm. Minor physiologic variation (95–102 bpm). No ectopic beats, no AV block, no bundle branch block.
interpretation.axis: Normal axis ~+50°. P axis ~60°, QRS axis ~50°, T axis ~45°. No axis deviation.

conduction.QRS_interpretation: Normal narrow QRS (<120ms). No bundle branch block, no pre-excitation.
conduction.QTc_interpretation: Normal (QTc <440ms in men, <460ms in women). Rate-appropriate shortening vs prior recording.

interpretation.p_waves: Upright in I, II, aVF. Inverted in aVR. Normal morphology, duration ~80ms, amplitude ~0.10 mV in II. Normal sinus P waves.
interpretation.qrs_complex: Narrow (84ms). Good R-wave progression V1→V5 (R increases from 0.12→1.40 mV). Transition zone at V3. No pathological Q waves. No delta waves. No LVH voltage criteria met.
interpretation.st_segments: Isoelectric in all leads. No ST elevation or depression. No acute ischemic changes.
interpretation.t_waves: Upright in I, II, III, aVF, V2–V6. Flat/slightly negative in V1 (normal). Inverted in aVR (normal). No T-wave inversion in lateral leads.
notable_findings: Sinus tachycardia — most clinically significant finding
No ST-T changes suggestive of ischemia
Recording artifact at start (4648 left, lead placement) and end (4651 right, lead removal)

comparison_to_prior_ekg.hr_change: +21 bpm (sinus tachycardia vs normal sinus rhythm)
comparison_to_prior_ekg.morphology_changes: QRS amplitudes broadly similar. QT appropriately shorter (320ms vs ~380ms) due to faster rate. No new ST or T-wave changes.

interpretation.overall_assessment: Sinus tachycardia at 99 bpm. Otherwise normal 12-lead ECG. Clinical correlation recommended to determine cause of tachycardia.
